content.title: Sterling K. Brown Reveals Paradise’s 3-Season Plan
content.text: Dan Fogelman doesn't want his post-apocalyptic mystery Paradise to overstay its welcome on Hulu.According to series star Sterling K. Brown—who previously worked with Fogelman on This Is Us—the show already has a definitive three-season arc mapped out (season two premieres in late February).Paradise star Sterling K. Brown talks three-season arc for hit Hulu series"So, twice in a row now, we've done this, where with This Is Us, he knew it was going to be six seasons," the actor told Collider at Brazil's CCXP. "[With] Paradise, he knows it's three seasons. It means that he gets to build towards something with each episode. We're not trying to put filler into something just to keep it going in perpetuity. We get to build towards something. I think the audience senses the momentum that each episode has serious consequences to it, and it's building to a complete picture."Season one ended with Secret Service Agent Xavier Collins (Brown) learning that the world outside the mountain bunker is still habitable for life. Instead of allowing the world's global powers to nuke the planet into oblivion, the late President Cal Bradford (James Marsden) activated a fail safe mechanism that rendered all missiles inert before they could detonate.Armed with that knowledge, Xavier set out in a plane to find his wife, Teri (Enuka Okuma), whom he assumed was long dead. But even if she's still alive and the air outside is breathable, post-apocalyptic fiction has taught us one very important lesson over the years: A free-for-all existence without the structure of civilized society can be just as dangerous as an irradiated wasteland."I think in film, and I think in theater, you get a chance to know the beginning, middle, and end, and I think it's incredibly satisfying to know the arc," Brown continued. "I find it very satisfying to know that we're starting at a place, we're ending at a very different place, and it feels complete. It feels whole. I'm excited. I don't think I ever want to do TV that is open-ended. That's a big, bold thing that's probably gonna keep me from a lot of jobs, but there's incredible satisfaction in building towards something."Aside from Brown and Okuma, returning faces from season include Julianne Nicholson (Sinatra), Sarah Shahi (Gabriela Torabi), Nicole Brydon Bloom (Jane Discroll), Krys Marshall (Nicole Robinson), Aliyah Mastin (Presley Collins), Percy Daggs IV (James Collins), and Charlie Evans (Jeremy Bradford). Marsden is a recurring guest star along with Shailene Woodley, Thomas Doherty, and Jon Beavers.Both Fogelman and Brown serve as executive producers on the show, as do Jess Rosenthal, John Hoberg, Steve Beers, Glenn Ficarra, and John Requa.When does season two of Paradise premiere?The first three episodes of Paradise season two will debut on Hulu Monday, Feb. 23. Subsequent installments will drop on a weekly basis after that.
